properties.name: MEASURED 2026-10-02 (0.77.0), limitation 13 PARTLY overturned. A local hub DOES carry a member list the door can read, its declared dependencies (`upstream_status` walked both under --call). What it lacks is where each child's STORE is on this machine, so a door agent can tell that a child moved but cannot open it. The served hub skill names only the MCP configuration as the list
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh), triage agent A, on limitation 13 of art:vscode-call-door-field-report-2026-10-02 ("A hub has no member list. The served hub skill says a local hub's list is the session's MCP config; under --call there is none, so the list must live elsewhere (a project file of store paths, for now)").

① OBSERVED (scratch hub `h` and child `c`, all through `--call`). The child was exported to child-export.json. The hub declared `external_dependency` dep:child (graph_id, design_export = that file) and dep:child-live (design_address = http://127.0.0.1:47911/, the child served with `--http` on a fixed port; the baseline was taken live, 2 nodes). `--call upstream_status` on the hub then reported `designs_declared: 2`, a finding per child, `kind` moved or unchanged. The hub's reply is a list of its members by id, with how each is watched. Log: /home/ajs7/.claude/jobs/fa666a94/tmp/triage-A/measure.log (HUB-*).
The served hub skill (get_skill hub, fetched 2026-10-02), section 1: "A local hub. A small design of its own (what it watches in each child, and which version it last aligned with) plus one connection per child design in the session's MCP configuration. That configuration is the list."

② PRECEDENT: upstream.rs's module doc, "Why the child list is the manifest … the dependency manifest already holds the list — checked in, version-pinned, naming each design by graph_id". dec:until-designs-share-a-server-the-cross-design-check-runs-at-the-hub (a search across "every design it tracks", accepted 2026-09-28, not yet served: find_tools for it returns only search_design). The pointer's `[[also]]` entries (dec:the-pointer-file-is-dot-reflow2-toml-and-the-first-slice-attaches-one-design) list other designs by id, address and role, and are never opened.

③/④ CANDIDATES: (a) no list exists without an MCP config (the reporter's reading); (b) the list exists as the manifest, and the skill text names the wrong source; (c) the list exists, but none of its entries says how to OPEN that member here.
(a) refuted by the measurement. (b) confirmed by the skill text against upstream.rs. (c) confirmed: a declaration carries `source` (free text), `design_export` (a file to fingerprint) or `design_address` (a server URL). Nothing holds "this child's store is at <path> on this machine", and `--call` opens exactly one `--graph-path`. The reporter's workaround, "a project file of store paths", is therefore filling (c), not (a).

⑥ CLASS: two halves of one model written at different times. The skill describes the hub as Claude Code sees it (several MCP connections, one session). The code and the 09-28 decision describe it as its own design sees it (the manifest). The door has only the second. Under the accepted blueprint (dec:idea-one-blueprint-the-store-is-the-design-and-an-export-is-a-perishable-photocopy: "a child is watched by asking its server (address), never a file"), the durable way to reach a member is its server address. A local store path is a per-machine fact, which is idea 13 (a hub address book).

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the skill's MCP-config wording should change now or wait for the hub-wide search tool.
